title.en: Changes around us: day and night

text.en: Two friends meet after a long time. Aparna is taller, her hair is short and Saba plays the guitar. So much has changed since last year.

Changes happen to us and the world all the time. Some take years, some days or minutes. You grow taller, leaves fall and grow again, flowers bloom and dry up, and the sky changes colour.
Think about the changes in yourself, your friends, your school and your surroundings since Grades 3 and 4.
Day changes into night and night into day. The Sun seems to rise in the east, move across the sky and set in the west. But is the Sun moving?
Game: one child is the Sun at the centre and another is the Earth, who turns slowly. While seeing the Sun, the Earth says day. When the Sun is out of view, it says night.
With a torch and a globe: the torchlight is the Sun. The side where light falls has day and the other side has night. Rotate the globe slowly and watch the day and night sides change.
Like the torch, the Sun stays in one place and it is the Earth that rotates.
A globe is a model of our Earth. Its blue parts are seas and oceans, which cover about three-fourths of the Earth. Seas are smaller and partly enclosed by land, oceans are vast and open. The rest is land with the countries.
Dong in Arunachal Pradesh is called India's First Village of the Sunrise because it is the first place the Sun's rays touch Indian land each morning.
(additional, not in the textbook) When it is day in India, it is night in countries on the other side of the Earth.

problem.en: Why do we have day and night?

text.en: The Sun stays in one place.
The Earth rotates.
The side facing the Sun has day, the other has night.

prompt.en: Explain day and night using a torch and a globe.

requiredIdeas.en: Lit side has day, dark side night

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the Sun goes around the Earth every day

points.en: Changes happen over minutes, days and years.
The Earth rotates, so we get day and night.
